articles.title: a16z is challenging Silicon Valley’s love for drop-outs by launching a school
articles.description: This academy for promising high school grads is somewhere between a trade school, Y Combinator, and Peter Thiel's Fellowship Program.
articles.summary: A16z, a major Silicon Valley venture capital firm, is launching an academy aimed at high school graduates to challenge the prevalent culture of dropouts in the tech industry. The program seeks to provide training and opportunities for young talent, potentially shifting the industry's values.
points: A16z's new academy is designed to train and support high school graduates in the tech industry, providing a pathway for those who may not have otherwise had such opportunities.

The academy aims to counteract the tech industry's acceptance of dropouts and its preference for self-taught individuals, potentially setting a new standard for educational background and preparation.
With the inclusion of a 5-year plan, the academy emphasizes long-term career development, offering a significant counter-narrative to the industry's typical 2-3 year trajectory.
articles.insight: The launch of A16z's academy could signify a cultural shift in the tech industry towards valuing formal education and sustained career development, challenging the status quo of self-taught expertise and dropout success stories.
